question:
According to Labour and Employment Statistics 2022, match the states in the first column with their rate of unemployment in the year 2020-21 given in the second column.

<div class="min-h-8 text-message flex w-full flex-col items-end gap-2 whitespace-normal break-words text-start [.text-message+&]:mt-5" data-message-author-role="assistant" data-messag

options.text: i) a, ii) c, iii) d, iv) b
i) d, ii) b, iii) c, iv) a
i) d, ii) c, iii) b, iv) a
i) b, ii) d, iii) a, iv) c

solution:
The correct answer is __**i) b, ii) d, iii) a, iv) c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** had an unemployment rate of **10.1%** in the year 2020-21, reflecting high joblessness in the state.
 
• **Goa** experienced an unemployment rate of **10.5%** during the same period, indicating significant employment challenges.
 
• **Haryana** had a lower unemployment rate of **6.3%**, which was comparatively better among the listed states.
 
• **Uttarakhand** had an unemployment rate of **6.9%**, positioning it in the mid-range among the states mentioned.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Labour and Employment Statistics** report is a vital source of information on the employment and unemployment scenario in India, providing insights into the economic health of the states.
 
• **Unemployment rate** is defined as the percentage of the labor force that is jobless and actively seeking employment.
 
• The **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** measures the proportion of the working-age population that is either working or actively looking for work.
 
• The **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** conducts periodic surveys to gather data on employment and unemployment, which is crucial for policy-making and economic planning.
 
• **Covid-19 pandemic** has significantly impacted employment rates across states, exacerbating joblessness and altering economic dynamics.
